name: The Tamarinds of Wat Arun's Giants

location.address: Wat Arun Ratchawararam, Thanon Wang Doem, Bangkok Yai (gate of the ordination hall)

verified_sources: https://spacebar.th/lifestyle/six-legendary-heritage-tree (2024-06-22, says the pair still stands beside the giants)
https://thestandard.co/trees-over-100-years-old-in-bkk/ (2020-10-21, says the two were not planted together)

official_register.name: Rukkha Moradok khong Phaendin (Heritage Trees of the Land), Dept of Cultural Promotion, Ministry of Culture, 2017 list no. 10

access: Paid entry to Wat Arun: foreign visitors pay a small cash fee at the ticket counter by the gate (amount not verified), open daily 8:00 to 18:00 (watarunvisit.com); one ticket covers the ordination hall and the gate with the giants. Shoes off inside the hall. Dress code not verified.

location_site.name: Gate of the ordination hall (ubosot), Wat Arun, with the two giant guardians

story:
These two tamarinds at Wat Arun share one entry in Thailand's heritage register, and they were not planted together.

They stand at the gate of the ordination hall, one beside each of the temple's giant guardians. The older grows next to Thotsakan, the green giant on the left. The Ministry of Culture, which listed the pair in 2017, says this tree already appears in a drawing by Henri Mouhot, the French naturalist whose Travels in Siam, Cambodia and Laos covers 1858 to 1860, and in a photograph from 1867. That is the register's own reading of the drawing, and it makes the left-hand tree more than 165 years old.

Its partner beside Sahatsadecha, the white giant on the right, was probably planted later. It first turns up on a postcard from the reign of Rama VII, between 1925 and 1934. So the pair is an old tree and a younger companion.

Nobody has recorded an age, girth or height for either, and both are clipped into the same neat shape. If you have an old picture of this gate, compare it with the left-hand trunk and tell us what you find.

Wat Arun charges foreign visitors a small cash fee at the counter by the gate and opens daily from 8:00 to 18:00. One ticket covers the hall and the giants. Shoes come off inside the hall. The cross-river ferry from Tha Tien pier lands you on the temple's side of the Chao Phraya.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise them by the giant guardian statues beside them, green Thotsakan on the left with the older tree, white Sahatsadecha on the right. They stand at the gate of the ordination hall, both clipped neat.
